raw_case_text:
A 66-year-old Asian Indian male presented with a history of high-grade fever with chills and rigors, severe arthralgia, popular skin rash, and fatigue. He was diagnosed with Chikungunya fever based on IgM-positive results from his serum sample. Investigations revealed erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 34 mm at the end of 1 h, platelet counts of 150,000/mm3, hemoglobin of 13 g/dL, and total leukocyte count of 12,000/mm3. The patient received treatment elsewhere for the condition including supportive management by antipyretic agents, fluids, and supportive therapy. For arthritis, the patient was also advised oral hydroxychloroquine. Due to significant fluid loss and severe disease, the patient also developed acute renal failure requiring dialysis. Fifteen days after the onset of fever, the patient developed decreased vision and photophobia in both eyes. However, the visual symptoms were not further evaluated at this time given his systemic comorbidities.
Six weeks after the onset of fever, the patient presented to the Ophthalmology department for further evaluation of decreased vision, which remained persistent. Detailed examination revealed best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) of 20/60 in the right eye (OD) and 20/30 in the left eye (OS). No relative afferent pupillary defect was apparent. Slit-lamp examination showed the absence of inflammation in the anterior chamber. There was no evidence of vitritis at this time. Intraocular pressure was 12 mmHg in OD and 13 mmHg in OS. The dilated fundus examination of the OD showed the presence of peripapillary areas of depigmented healed retinitis lesions with retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) alterations. Similar lesions were seen near the inferior arcade and temporally. The macula was spared [Fig. 1]. The patient had the presence of a dense nuclear cataract in OD. Autofluorescence imaging (FAF) showed stippled irregular hypoautofluorescence in the nasal peripapillary lesions and hyperautofluorescence in the lesions inferiorly. The OS showed the presence of a healed macular lesion with RPE alterations and hypoautofluorescence on FAF imaging. There was an area of hyperautofluorescence at the superior arcade near the optic nerve head [Fig. 1].
OCT scans through the macula in OD showed a normal foveal contour with relative preservation of all the retinal layers. There were few hyperreflective foci in the inner retinal layers causing subtle back-shadowing on OCT. OCT scan through the macula of OS showed the presence of outer retinal disruption (disruption of the external limiting membrane [ELM], ellipsoid, and myoid zone) and mild RPE elevation and focal thickening [Fig. 2]. OCTA of OD showed an irregular decrease in the SCP and DCP. In addition, the choriocapillaris slab on automatic segmentation revealed few subtle hyporeflective areas suggestive of flow deficit. In OS, the OCTA at the level of SCP and DCP showed a more significant loss of vascular density compared to OD. The choriocapillaris slab in OS showed discrete areas of hyporeflectivity suggestive of flow deficit, more obvious compared to OD [Fig. 3].
The patient was followed up with no ocular treatment (oral hydroxychloroquine, started 6 weeks ago, was continued), and was afebrile and asymptomatic systemically at this time. Ten weeks after the episode of Chikungunya fever, he was systemically well, and BCVA measured 20/50 in OD and 20/40 in OS. There was no further improvement of BCVA or change in the fundus/OCTA appearance at 4-month follow-up visit.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 66-year-old male presented with persistent bilateral decreased vision and photophobia 6 weeks after an acute febrile illness with rash and arthralgia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 66-year-old male experienced high-grade fever with chills, rigors, severe arthralgia, papular rash, and fatigue, complicated by severe dehydration and acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis. Fifteen days after fever onset, he developed decreased vision and photophobia in both eyes. The visual symptoms persisted, prompting ophthalmologic evaluation 6 weeks after initial fever onset.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recent acute febrile illness complicated by acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis; prior treatment with antipyretics, intravenous fluids, and oral hydroxychloroquine.
subjective.review_of_systems: Bilateral photophobia, decreased vision, fatigue, residual arthralgia. Medications: Oral hydroxychloroquine. Allergies: Not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Ophthalmologic examination: BCVA 20/60 OD, 20/30 OS; no relative afferent pupillary defect; intraocular pressure: 12 mmHg OD, 13 mmHg OS. Slit-lamp exam: No anterior chamber inflammation or vitritis; dense nuclear cataract in OD. Dilated fundus examination: OD showed peripapillary depigmented healed retinitis lesions with retinal pigment epithelial (RPE) alterations, similar lesions near the inferior arcade and temporally, macula spared; OS showed healed macular lesion with RPE alterations and hyperautofluorescence at the superior arcade near the optic nerve head.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin: 13 g/dL; total leukocyte count: 12,000/mm3; platelet count: 150,000/mm3; ESR: 34 mm at 1 hour.
objective.advanced_workup: Fundus autofluorescence (FAF): Stippled irregular hypoautofluorescence in nasal peripapillary lesions and hyperautofluorescence inferiorly in OD; hypoautofluorescence in macular lesion and hyperautofluorescence at superior arcade in OS. Optical coherence tomography (OCT): OD showed normal foveal contour with inner retinal hyperreflective foci; OS showed outer retinal disruption (ELM, ellipsoid, and myoid zone) with mild RPE elevation and focal thickening. Optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA): OD demonstrated irregular decrease in superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexus (DCP) and subtle flow deficit in choriocapillaris; OS showed significant vascular density loss at SCP/DCP and discrete flow deficits in choriocapillaris.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmation: Serum IgM antibody positive for Chikungunya virus, confirming post-Chikungunya retinitis and macular neuroretinopathy. Management and course: Managed conservatively without active ocular therapy; ongoing oral hydroxychloroquine continued for residual arthritis. At 10-week follow-up, BCVA improved slightly to 20/50 OD and 20/40 OS, remaining stable at 4 months without progression.
